suites.description: An AFIDL import names an exact SpecificationId and nothing else. Covers the import grammar itself, which admits only ns-segment ('.' ns-segment)* '@' MAJOR as its target: there is no syntactic position for a version range, a path, a wildcard or a per-type alias, so the rejected forms are rejected by the grammar rather than by a post-hoc check.

Import resolution is a pure function of the source and an explicitly supplied in-memory universe: af-idl has no filesystem, network, registry or clock dependency at all, so a latest-version or network lookup is not merely discouraged but unrepresentable in the crate's dependency set.

Import declarations never enter canonical identity: the canonical TypeSchema record keeps exactly its three members schema/name/body, and no import alias can appear in a NamedRef. Covers the frozen import equivalence groups (alias rename, import order, unused import) and the structural audit of the canonical model.

Component identity, all thirteen semantic fields and full Effect Atom identity define canonical contract bytes. Publication version, implementation identity, price and diagnostics are excluded. Expected bytes and HashV1 values are generated by the independent Python component-contract oracle.

Component substitution preserves separate directional proofs. Exact I/O sets and nominal pins are the positive v1 subset; required-input/output breaks violate and unsupported relations remain Unproven.

Single-component validation composes exact I/O/R/F/epsilon/K/U/X checks with explicit relation snapshots. Open and unknown rows, missing catalog coverage and missing meter coordinates fail closed; non-Proven subproofs remain visible in the report.

Phase 4B.1 adds exactly the ComponentContract and three accepted relation schemas, with additive ABI and no new HashV1 domain or Semantic IR change. Existing schemas and prior corpus fixtures remain byte-identical.

Three standalone relation catalogs have closed exact schemas, canonical typed content and checksums over ACE1 bytes. A proof records schema, opaque revision and content checksum; changed catalog content cannot reuse an old result.

A standalone Python oracle generates 72 vectors for the four existing advanced control opcodes, nested propagation, typed carry/output interfaces, the preserved Scope CaseId, and boundary failures. Scope is now supported by Phase 4B.2B.3; only its formerly unsupported Expected changed under revision 2. Every vector runs through checked Semantic IR, Phase 3C, leaf resolution and the production analyzer; output, static multiplicity, Flow dependencies, Recovery proof state and overflow are compared without runtime simulation.
Failure, Effect, Flow, Usage, Resource, Recovery and Execution use their separate frozen algebras or source-scoped summaries; unknown is never treated as empty.
Unordered summary inputs normalize deterministically while the frozen SEQUENCE child order remains semantic.
Equal contract digests and AtomKeys do not merge logical call sites; control provenance retains source nodes and row ordinals.
The frozen all/fail_fast modes retain sibling effects and usage, keep explicit branch-output and resource mappings, and do not aggregate X into one Worker.
The derived summary is not a checked component contract and creates no control digest, runtime state, grant, handle, plan, journal, reducer or worker placement.
Inherited Violation, Unproven and RequiresEvidence statuses are retained alongside any derived envelope; unsupported operators never default to empty.
A standalone Python oracle computes the frozen control vectors without invoking Rust or introducing a persistence format.
RACE is first-terminal and conservatively accumulates every contestant's effect, usage, failure and recovery facts without choosing a static winner.
SELECT uses exclusive joins, full guard/qualifier identities, exact typed interfaces, and explicit unresolved selector coverage/decision influence.
SEQUENCE preserves child order, uses formal Effect/Usage accumulation, weakens conditional lower bounds, and retains Phase 3C cross-sibling dataflow evidence.
AWAIT keeps its exact signal pin and correlation, explicit unknown external provenance, missing adapter obligations, and the absence of implicit timeout or business failure.
ComponentContract semantic digest stability is separated from checked proof reuse, which is bound to the exact context object and relation content.
Analysis is deterministic for one exact snapshot and source presentation-only metadata does not alter semantic identity.
Exact INVOKE target resolution, checked contract pinning, exact public input/output port typing, required coverage, Phase 3C producer/scope reuse, and distinct call-site identity.
Exact resource requirement-port to ResourceSlotId mapping, explicit alias groups, missing attribute evidence, and source-preserving scoped Effect and Flow mappings.
The phase resolves only one leaf and cannot create runtime authority or close SEQUENCE, SELECT, PARALLEL, RACE, ITERATE, RETRY, TIMEOUT, HANDLE, SCOPE, or compensation contracts.
A standalone Python implementation computes exact target, port/resource, scoped effect, subflow, context and verdict expectations without calling Rust or defining a wire ABI.
Scoped leaf summaries retain full source contract dimensions, Effect atom identity and qualifiers, flow provenance, per-call U/K/X boundaries, and exact proof-context references.
CALL_SUBFLOW reuses exact Phase 3D targets and interface checks, requires a complete checked export, separates declaration from body proof, and checks exact-digest dependency closure.

An independent Python oracle differentially checks the exact non-wire RootExportAssertion pins, typed I/O/R/E/F/K/X maps, nine static dimensions, proof-context invalidation and subflow/body separation. Every declared case executes checked Semantic IR, Phase 3C, leaf resolution, root derivation, RootRecoverySummary, and the production RootExport checker.

An independent Python oracle differentially checks typed K-to-epsilon guards, LocalActionBound/RootActionBound, exact source/action/profile multisets, operator-specific root folds, root epsilon/Recovery-Usage coverage, and stage-gated counterexamples without implementing RootExportAssertion.

An independent Python oracle generates 55 Scope, exact K-derived conditional compensation, and nested control-tree vectors. Every case runs through checked IR, Phase 3C, production leaf resolution, the production algebra, and root closure; mutations cover resource proof, compensation bound, traversal order, and source accounting.
Fixed rational rates use checked integer arithmetic and the safe per-meter-unit ceiling rule; aggregate-once rounding is rejected because it can underestimate independently rounded requests.
targets: af-usage project_cost and checked ceil arithmetic

suites.description: Cost Projection is static only: explicit currency and atomic money, complete by-value fixed price snapshots, meter/unit coverage, forward/recovery cost bounds and static budget proofs. Missing price is Unproven, never free, and no billing or ledger authority exists.

Phase 4A.5B adds one additive Cost Projection AFIDL module and its ABI/corpus entries but no HashV1 domain; all prior TypeSchemaDigests, SemanticIrDigest, Usage Signature and previous corpora remain unchanged.
targets: af-usage cost static surface audit (no digest/ledger/runtime)

suites.description: Cross-domain digest separation: the same payload hashed under every frozen HashV1 domain yields pairwise-distinct digests. Covers the af-core property test over the full registry and the frozen matrix in spec/conformance/digest/domain-separation.json.

Effect operation resolution happens against an explicit, immutable, in-memory catalog universe only: af-effect has no registry lookup, no latest-version fallback, no filesystem/network discovery and no default catalog, so an unresolved operation can only fail closed. Covers the crate dependency audit and the unknown-operation corpus.
targets: af-effect crate dependency set (af-core, af-idl, af-semantic)

suites.description: An effect signature is never authority: the crate has no EffectGrant/EffectIntent/EffectReceipt/Effect Gateway/Credential Broker/Provider Dispatch symbol, no execution surface, and the unknown row carries no capability material. Covers the static absence audit over the crate source and the frozen top-row corpus.
targets: af-effect static surface audit (no grant/receipt/gateway symbols)

suites.description: The effect layer is static only: no af-ir dependency, no I/O, clock, randomness, async runtime, policy engine, credential broker or provider; control propagation is a pure function over signatures. Covers the crate dependency audit and the source surface.
targets: af-effect static surface audit (no runtime/journal/plan symbols)

suites.description: The retry envelope conservatively scales the logical bounds by the physical attempt ceiling and records the obligation that narrowing requires a recovery contract: no idempotency qualifier is exploited this phase. Covers the retry algebra corpus and the envelope shape.

Phase 4A.1 added exactly one AFIDL module and no HashV1 domain: the canonical effect signature has ACE1 bytes but no digest, the semantic-ir module stays byte-identical, and every pre-existing corpus digest is unchanged. Covers the static surface audits and the zero-drift corpus runs.
Execution compatibility freezes separate placement-feasibility and security-preservation directions and combines them only after both verdicts are available.
Static profile matching checks all hard constraints and keeps rejection, unproven evidence and descriptor proof distinct; soft preferences never compensate for a hard failure.

Execution Requirements is static only: explicit capability, quantity, sandbox, trust, residency, runtime and ABI constraints are not workers, advertisements, admission, leases, reservations, scheduler state or authority.
Phase 4A.7 adds one additive Execution Requirements AFIDL module and ABI/corpus entries but no HashV1 domain or X digest; all prior schema digests and static corpora remain unchanged.
targets: af-execution static surface audit (no digest/runtime symbols)

suites.description: The five non-failure planes are structurally outside the Failure Row: no TimedOut/Cancelled/RecoveryBlocked/TaskAttemptLost/RuntimeIncident failure type exists anywhere in af-failure, the frozen HandleMatch carries timed_out as a payload-less unit case beside the typed failure matcher, and TIMEOUT/AWAIT compositions add no type. Covers the static absence audit and the read-only HandleMatch consistency check.
targets: af-failure static surface audit (no control-outcome failure types)

suites.description: INVOKE and CALL_SUBFLOW failure propagation is deferred to the ComponentContract stage: the analysis-level Unproven envelope fails closed (failure_row_unproven) and a missing explicit FailureRow is never assumed empty. Covers the Unproven corpus case and the static surface.

The failure layer is static only: no af-ir, af-effect or af-spec dependency, no I/O, clock, randomness, async runtime, worker transport or mapping adapter; propagation is a pure function over rows. Covers the crate dependency audit and the source surface.
targets: af-failure crate dependency set (af-core, af-idl, af-semantic)
af-failure static surface audit (no runtime/journal/plan symbols)

suites.description: Failure matching is exact nominal identity only: no error-message or error-code substring matching, no exception class-name reflection, no provider-specific mapping, and no same-short-name or same-shape containment inference. Covers the static audit over the crate source and the same-short-name corpus.
targets: af-failure static surface audit (no string/reflection matching)

suites.description: Phase 4A.2 added exactly one AFIDL module and no HashV1 domain: no FailureRowDigest exists, semantic-ir.afidl stays byte-identical, the effect corpus stays at revision 2, and every pre-existing corpus digest is unchanged. Covers the static surface audits and the zero-drift corpus runs.
Exact successor nominal source registration only; no production capture or capability.
Closed source/site/body/rank/stage registration and bounded manual subgraphs; no production binder or positive capability.

Provenance, trust, taint and information flow stay four distinct concepts: no trust score, no single trusted flag; confidentiality restrictions and taints are separate nominal types; unknown provenance is never trusted and unknown taint is never the empty set. Covers the static absence audit and the label/summary corpus cases.
targets: af-flow static surface audit (no trust-score symbols)

suites.description: Taint propagation is may-influence conservative: union algebra properties frozen, pure expressions inherit all input taints, unknown influence stays unknown, and no incomplete influence list can prove a real influence away. Covers the propagation corpus family and the static surface.

A declared flow ceiling is not an observed flow and not a policy approval: judgments are ProvenWithinDeclaredCeiling / RequiresTrustedTransformation / Unproven only, no PolicyDecision substitute exists anywhere in af-flow, and referencing an effect sink is not being granted it. Covers the static absence audit and the sink corpus cases.
targets: af-flow static surface audit (no grant/policy symbols)

suites.description: Data egress and decision influence are separate flow kinds judged separately: the non-relaxation proof never compares ceilings across kinds, and the two golden sink cases freeze the distinction. Covers the flow-kind rules and the compatibility corpus.

The LLM strong taint mixer: all model-visible inputs may influence all model outputs; output taint is the union of every visible input taint plus model_generated, influence stays unknown, authority is never elevated, and a model output is never endorsed. Covers the mixer corpus cases and the static surface.

No automatic declassification, no automatic endorsement, persistence does not imply trust: the wire model expresses no taint-deleting or restriction-lowering operation, ordinary transformations (store/load/serialize/summarize) never endorse, and this phase records at most requires_declassification / requires_endorsement obligations. Covers the persistence corpus cases and the static absence audit.
targets: af-flow static surface audit (no declassify/endorse execution)

suites.description: No confidentiality hierarchy is invented: containment is set membership plus explicit catalog rules, there is no total order over user-defined labels from which downgrade flows could be claimed, and undecidable containment is Unproven rather than resolved by an invented subtyping. Covers the non-relaxation corpus and the static surface.

External-effect sinks reuse the structured EffectOperationRef by exact cross-module identity, resolve fail-closed against the explicit catalog, are classified only by the catalog (never by operation name), and referencing an effect is not being granted it. Covers the sink corpus cases and the read-only consistency audit over the effect module.

Phase 4A.4 added exactly one AFIDL module and no HashV1 domain: no InformationFlowDigest exists, semantic-ir.afidl stays byte-identical, the effect corpus stays at revision 2, the failure corpus at revision 1, the resource corpus at revision 1, and every pre-existing corpus digest is unchanged. Covers the static surface audits and the zero-drift corpus runs.
targets: af-flow static surface audit (no flow digest)

suites.description: Independent Python and Rust production conformance for the registered portable proof-input schema, canonical ACE1 codec, closed D0-D4 decoder, inline content identities, reference closure and exact static semantic-support selection. No context reconstruction or RootExport revalidation is asserted by this suite.
Unknown and partially-applied effects fail closed: blind retry is forbidden, reconciliation evidence is required, and static proof distinguishes Proven, RequiresEvidence, Unproven and Violation.

Recovery Contract is static only: replay/idempotency declarations, exact EffectAtom clauses, reconciliation and compensation obligations are not receipts, grants, runtime decisions or business failures.
Phase 4A.6 adds one additive Recovery AFIDL module and ABI/corpus entries but no HashV1 domain, receipt, runtime or journal surface; all prior TypeSchemaDigests and corpora remain unchanged.

A resource requirement is a declaration of need, never a grant: satisfaction is a static predicate over explicit descriptors, no requirement-satisfied-implies-grant path exists anywhere in af-resource, and the capability ceiling / effect grant / requirement distinction is enforced by the static absence audit. Covers the authority-distinction rules and the crate source audit.
targets: af-resource static surface audit (no grant/capability symbols)

suites.description: Resource-type recognition is an explicit registry-level fact: the universe is explicit, read-only, in-memory input; a legal AFIDL schema alone is not a resource type; there is no latest-schema lookup, no fallback and no implicit upcast. Covers the universe corpus cases and the static surface.

Requirement rows are never merged across components: port numbers are local to one contract interface, equal port numbers do not name the same resource, and no union/merge operation exists in af-resource. Aggregation requires an explicit port mapping at the later contract-analysis stage. Covers the cross-namespace corpus case and the static absence audit.
targets: af-resource static surface audit (no merge/union symbols)

suites.description: The resource layer is static only: no af-ir, af-effect, af-failure or af-spec dependency, no I/O, clock, randomness, async runtime, network, credential, adapter or binding; satisfaction and non-strengthening are pure functions over explicit values. Covers the crate dependency audit and the source surface.
targets: af-resource crate dependency set (af-core, af-idl, af-semantic)
af-resource static surface audit (no runtime symbols)

suites.description: Resource-type matching is exact nominal identity only: the full (SpecificationId, TypeName, pinned TypeSchemaDigest) triple; the same short name under a different specification or with a different digest is a DIFFERENT resource type, in satisfaction and in compatibility alike. No implicit subtyping exists. Covers the same-short-name corpus cases and the changed-type compatibility cases.

Phase 4A.3 added exactly one AFIDL module and no HashV1 domain: no resource-requirement digest exists, semantic-ir.afidl stays byte-identical, the effect corpus stays at revision 2, the failure corpus at revision 1, and every pre-existing corpus digest is unchanged. Covers the static surface audits and the zero-drift corpus runs.
targets: af-resource static surface audit (no digest domains)

suites.description: The expression body set is closed to the fifteen Phase 3A expressions and to the workflow primitive universe. Covers the exhaustive match over ExpressionBody in the Rust checker and the closed SemanticPrimitiveType enum, whose ALL table and keyword round-trip are asserted in-tree.

Value availability is per use site and dominance is the structured transfer: a producer dominates a use exactly when the opcode-specific environment places the produced slot into that use site's EntryValues. Covers the frozen positive/negative dataflow corpus and the per-use-site expression reuse fixture.

SELECT cases, PARALLEL branches, RACE branches and HANDLE clauses are mutually isolated: ordinals are identity keys, never execution order, and a raw child output never escapes its wrapper. Covers the branch-isolation negative corpus.

The analysis artifact is derived-only: it is a plain Rust projection, never ACE1-encoded, never hashed into the SemanticIrDigest, and absent from AFIDL, the ABI registry and the wire model. Covers the static audit of the canonical path and the golden digest invariance run.

Loop-local values never escape their iterate: the foreach source and carry initials evaluate from the pre-loop environment, the body sees item and carry slots, the while guard never reads a body output, and item/carry/body-output slots are invisible outside the loop. Covers the iterate negative corpus.

The analysis runs strictly after Phase 3B validation: every Phase 3B negative keeps its exact expected error kind, and every Phase 3C negative passes Phase 3B and is rejected only by the analysis. Covers both frozen negative corpora and their rejected_at markers.

Resource lexical visibility: the root sees every declared slot, SCOPE attenuates to exactly its listed subset, narrowing ends at the scope boundary, and invoke/call_subflow uses require lexical visibility. Covers the resource positive and negative corpus.

Phase 3C froze every durable surface: semantic-ir.afidl byte-identical at its Phase 3B registry digest, exactly four AFIDL modules, 232 ABI rows (100 semantic IR), 14 HashV1 domains, and the 13 ComputationBody cases unchanged. Covers the static surface audit.
Workflow outputs read only run parameters and the root's own outputs: WorkflowExitValues = RunParameterSlots + Exports(root), frozen per positive case.

CallComposite and Trigger never reach the canonical IR: the 13-case ComputationBody variant is closed, so an authoring construct or a deployment binding is structurally inexpressible. Covers the static absence audit over the crate source and the schema module.
AWAIT has no built-in timeout: the AwaitBody schema carries only signal_type and correlation, so timing is expressed by composing TIMEOUT(AWAIT(...)). Covers the schema shape and the static audit.

COMPENSATION_SCOPE holds no compensation task list and MUST NOT erase forward computation or effect history: the IR body is a single child reference, so there is nothing to erase with. Covers the model shape and the static audit.

Dataflow (expression reads a value slot) and ownership (a computation owns a child) are separate validator logics over separate edge sets: ComputationBody::children walks only child references, and expression checking stays in the semantic core. Covers the two code paths and their tests.

ComputationInterface is derived on demand from outputs and slot types; no second interface table is stored anywhere in the model or the corpus. Covers the static audit and the interface equality negatives.
targets: af-ir static surface audit (no interface table)

suites.description: No runtime object exists in the IR crate: no opcode state machine, no runtime command, no journal event, no occurrence identity, no worker/scheduler/reducer, no resource handle, no clock, no randomness, no network, no af-spec dependency. Covers the static absence audit over the dependency set and the source surface.

ValueSlotId and ResourceSlotId are distinct nominal types that may carry the same number. Covers the Rust newtype separation test and the corpus case where a value slot 1 and a resource slot 1 coexist in one document.
No new HashV1 domain is introduced in Phase 3A: the domain registry table still has exactly its frozen entries and the semantic layer computes no digest of its own.
No ResourceHandle, binding snapshot or runtime object exists in the semantic layer. Covers the static absence audit over the crate's public surface and the resource slot model.
targets: af-semantic resource slot model (logical requirement only)
static self-check: no runtime object in af-semantic

suites.description: Expressions are pure: no I/O, clock, randomness, environment, policy or registry query, resource access or effect. Covers the static purity audit over the closed expression body set and the absence of I/O dependencies in the crate.
targets: af-semantic (no I/O, clock, random or env dependency)
static self-check: closed expression body set

suites.description: A resource slot's definition is immutable for the document's life. Covered by the absence of any mutating operation in the resource model and by the checked document type being the only way to reach a resolved requirement.

Cross-document types compare structurally: primitives by keyword, schema leaves by exact TypeSchemaRef (identity and digest), containers recursively; local SemanticTypeIds never compare numerically. Covers the frozen corpus cases for renumbered type tables and same-id different-type rejections.

CALL_SUBFLOW resolves its target only by the exact pinned SemanticIrDigest in an explicit in-memory universe: fail closed on a missing digest, no latest fallback, no filesystem/network/deployment lookup, idempotent re-insertion of identical bytes. Covers the frozen target-resolution negatives and the digest pins.

The subflow interface is derived, canonical-key ordered and never durable: inputs from RunParameterId order, outputs from canonical name order, resources from every declared ResourceSlot in id order, 1-based independent namespaces, deterministic for a fixed digest. Covers the frozen interface projections and the equivalence groups.

The subflow pass consumes a checked document plus its own Phase 3C analysis and runs strictly after them: Phase 3B and Phase 3C error kinds never move, and a document without CALL_SUBFLOW passes against an empty universe. Covers the frozen corpus rejected_at layering and the zero-drift proofs for both earlier corpora.
Static Usage algebra is conservative and checked: additive accumulation, branch maximum join, repetition, explicit zero, unknown propagation and arithmetic overflow preserve sound upper bounds.

Control propagation accumulates all possible usage: retry amplifies by attempts, race retains loser consumption, compensation never refunds forward usage, and max_inflight is not a total iteration bound.

The Usage layer is declaration-only: explicit additive meter identity and units, finite/unbounded upper bounds, missing versus zero, static ceiling/non-increase proofs, and no measurement, billing, pricing, reservation, settlement, quota or runtime ledger. Covers Usage golden, negative and compatibility cases plus the static absence audit.

Phase 4A.5A adds exactly one Usage AFIDL module and additive ABI/corpus entries but no HashV1 domain; all pre-existing AFIDL TypeSchemaDigests, SemanticIrDigest, effect/failure/resource/information-flow corpora and ABI assignments remain unchanged.
targets: af-usage static surface audit (no digest domain)
